tags.validation_note: Re-audited 2026-08-12 with wreck deep-research (cross-check requirement): sinking (1987, Mauritius Conservation Society) confirmed across 5+ independent sources. Vessel length conflicts across sources (42m/44m/52m) -- widened range reported in markdown rather than picking one figure. Cyclone that righted the wreck identified specifically as Cyclone Dina (Jan 2002), corroborated by Wikipedia's cyclone record plus 2 dive-specific sources. No tonnage or build date found anywhere; not stated.

No source uses the name 'Flic en Flac Pass' as a named dive site. Local dive operators list Cathedral, Little Swiss, Rempart Serpent, Aquarium, Big Rock, Canyon for this area. This may be a fabricated or conflated site name. Only 1-2 aggregate databases (padi.com region page, scubasnap.app) reference it, not local operators. Re-checked 2026-08-12 with a fresh search -- same conclusion, still unresolved.

tags.validation_note: Re-audited 2026-08-12 with wreck deep-research (cross-check requirement): 2003 scuttling date reconfirmed directly against africatouroperators.org and consistent with prior sources. Organisations involved (Mauritius Marine Conservation Society / Mauritius Scuba Diving Association / Mauritius Oceanographic Institute) could not be independently re-confirmed this pass and are now flagged as unconfirmed in the markdown rather than stated as fact. IMPORTANT: vessel specs (314 gross tons, built 1979, ex-Fukuichi Maru No. 86) found in shipping databases belong to a sister vessel 'Hoi Siong No. 5', NOT this wreck (No. 6) -- explicitly excluded to avoid cross-vessel conflation. No verified length/tonnage/build date exists for Hoi Siong No. 6 itself.
